<USER_SCRIPT>
CORAL — A CITY LAUNCH

INT. DOWNTOWN APARTMENT BATHROOM - MORNING

Hard light off white tile. SCARLETT,
a city influencer in a black turtleneck,
unboxes a coral lipstick and turns it slowly to camera.

SCARLETT (V.O.)
One shade. One city.

CLOSE ON THE TUBE — the coral bullet twists up and catches the
light. Scarlett smiles at her reflection, the colour already hers.

EXT. DOWNTOWN SIDEWALK - CONTINUOUS

Scarlett walks a crowded crosswalk, taxis stacked at the light,
office glass behind her. She glances back at camera.

SCARLETT (V.O.)
Made for the street. Wear it everywhere.

EXT. ROOFTOP LEDGE - CONTINUOUS

She laughs as a train rattles past below. The lipstick lands
beside the brand mark on the concrete ledge.

SUPER:  CORAL.  OUT NOW.
</USER_SCRIPT>

Target video duration: 1 minute (about 8-12 clips). Group clips that share a location and beat into one scene — a scene may hold several shots. Each SHOT is one video clip. Clip durations MUST be 5–15 seconds — those are the only lengths the selected video model can render. Label every scene (e.g. a "Scene 3 — 5s" heading). When a scene has more than one shot, also label each shot (e.g. "Shot 1 — 5s"); shot labels in a scene MUST add up to the scene label. A one-shot scene needs only the scene label — that label IS the clip duration. The clip labels (shot labels when present, otherwise scene labels) MUST add up to 60 seconds (±2 seconds). Count the clips, add the labels, and do not return until they sum to the target. Reach the target through the number of shots, not by stretching illegal clip lengths. If the brief asks for a title card, logo, SUPER, or on-screen text, do not write that card — the image model cannot render text. Substitute a final living beat with a real subject. End with a single line: TOTAL: <sum>s

Style & genre (let this drive WHAT HAPPENS, not just the look):
- Style: Product Ad / ecommerce
- About: Fresh, tactile product content with lifestyle context and sensory detail. Designed for Instagram, DTC brands, e-commerce, and social-first campaigns.
- Genre cues: ecommerce, product, instagram, dtc, lifestyle, social

Style context (apply these aesthetics throughout):
- Mood: Fresh, sensory, and effortlessly cool
- Art style: Modern social-first product photography with tactile, editorial energy. Products shown in real-life context -- hands opening packaging, fingers pressing textures, products on bathroom shelves, kitchen counters, rumpled linen. Close-up detail shots emphasize material and finish. Flat-lays with curated minimal arrangements. Color-matched backgrounds that complement the product. Every frame feels like something you would screenshot and save
- Lighting: Bright natural window light with clean directional shadows. Direct on-camera flash for punchy editorial energy on select shots. No heavy diffusion -- let light feel real and immediate. Warm late-afternoon glow for lifestyle moments. High-key and airy overall with pops of contrast
- Color palette: #FFFFFF, #F0E6D3, #D4536D, #1A1A1A, #E8F4E8
- Color grading: Clean and bright with true-to-life color. Whites are crisp, skin tones warm and natural. Minimal processing -- the product looks like it does in your hand. Slight warmth in highlights, lifted shadows keeping everything airy. One accent color pops against neutral base
- Camera work: Dynamic mix of handheld and locked shots with consistent energy. Handheld with natural micro-movement for lifestyle moments -- hands interacting, daily rituals, real context. Quick-cut to locked beauty frames for hero product shots. Macro details on textures and surfaces. Overhead flat-lays directly above. Eye-level and slightly above angles. Shallow depth of field on tactile details. Energetic pacing -- no lingering, every frame earns its time
- Reference works: modern social-first skincare-brand content, dewy minimalist beauty-brand visual identity, sun-soaked lifestyle beauty campaigns, playful color-blocked skincare content

Aspect ratio: 16:9 landscape — favor wide, cinematic compositions

response.content:
Scene 1 — 18s

Shot 1 — 6s
INT. DOWNTOWN APARTMENT BATHROOM — MORNING. Hard sunlight cuts across white tile and a black stone sink. Scarlett, a sharp-eyed city influencer in a black turtleneck, tears open a coral lipstick carton with one hand while her phone buzzes beside it. The handheld camera drifts with her movement as she catches the tube before it rolls into the sink.

Shot 2 — 6s
Overhead on the sink: the coral lipstick, a silver metro card, black sunglasses, and a single green hair clip arranged on white tile. Scarlett’s hand sweeps the metro card aside, lifts the lipstick, and twists the coral bullet upward. A bright window reflection travels across its satin surface as the camera makes a quick, precise push-in.

Shot 3 — 6s
At the mirror, Scarlett applies the lipstick while fastening one earring with her other hand. She turns toward the window, testing the color in the hard morning light; the coral warms her face against the black turtleneck. She gives her reflection a quick, satisfied grin and says, “Good. Let’s go.”

Scene 2 — 22s

Shot 1 — 7s
EXT. DOWNTOWN SIDEWALK — MORNING. Scarlett bursts from a narrow apartment entrance into a moving crowd, one hand holding a coffee and the other gripping her phone. The camera tracks backward at street level as taxis slide through the background and her coral lips flash when she calls, “Sorry—coming through!”

Shot 2 — 7s
At the crosswalk, Scarlett pauses among commuters as the signal changes. A gust lifts the edge of her black coat; she catches it, tucks her phone into her pocket, and strides across the white stripes. The camera moves parallel with her, glass towers and yellow taxis streaking behind her while the coral color stays crisp in the center of frame.

Shot 3 — 8s
Outside a flower kiosk, Scarlett stops mid-stride as a vendor extends a small bunch of coral ranunculus toward her. She laughs, compares the flowers to her lips, then tucks one bloom into her coat pocket. A direct on-camera flash freezes the playful exchange before the camera swings with her as she heads back into the crowd.

Scene 3 — 12s

Shot 1 — 6s
EXT. DOWNTOWN ROOFTOP — LATE AFTERNOON. Scarlett climbs onto the rooftop, wind pushing her hair across her face as the city glows warm behind her. She pulls the coral lipstick from her pocket, checks the bullet, and twists it down with a decisive click while a distant train begins to rattle below.

Shot 2 — 6s
Wide cinematic view: Scarlett leans against the rooftop railing, the coral flower still tucked into her coat. She raises the lipstick toward the skyline, then lowers it and turns toward camera with an irrepressible smile as the passing train flashes through the streets beneath her. She takes one last step into the warm wind, the lipstick secure in her hand.

TOTAL: 52s
